Method of Attack: Exploitation of zero-day vulnerabilities in cryptographic protocols GG-18, GG-20, and Lindell17 allowing attackers to extract private keys by sending specially crafted messages and mishandling aborts in multi-party computation (MPC) protocols
Extraction of key shards in 16-bit chunks from GG18 and GG20 threshold signature schemes
Exploitation of mishandling of aborts in Lindell17 2PC protocol to extract private keys after multiple signature attempts
Asymmetric attack scenarios corrupting client or server to reveal secret key bits
Impacted Systems: Dozens of other cryptocurrency wallet providers using GG-18, GG-20, and Lindell17 MPC protocols
Attack Vector: Sending specially crafted messages to wallets implementing vulnerable MPC protocols
Exploiting lack of checks on Paillier modulus and encryption status
Mishandling of aborts forcing wallets to continue signing and leak key bits
Corrupting client or server to send commands or crafted messages
